title: Find the figure
brief: The answer sits in a chart, a diagram or a layout that text extraction flattens. How much meaning lives in visuals, whether you need text citations and the storage budget are open. Choose how pages and figures become searchable.

blocks.text: Four ways to index what a page shows

blocks.md: Azure AI Search documents two image paths [[r12]]. **Verbalize** with the GenAI Prompt skill, one LLM call per image, which supports hybrid text queries and citations. **Embed directly** with the Azure Vision or AML skill, which needs no LLM at index time and supports image-to-vector queries but gives no reasons or citation text. Mixed corpora often need both. A third idea skips parsing: embed the page image itself with a vision-language model (ColPali family) [[r14]]. The status of these features is mixed GA and preview as of 2026-10-13, so check each skill.

options.name: Parse, then text-embed
options.summary: OCR or layout extraction, then chunk and embed the text.
cons: Figures and layout are flattened or dropped
options.bestWhen: Meaning lives in prose and simple tables.
options.avoidWhen: The answer is in charts or spatial layout.

options.name: Caption, then embed
options.summary: An LLM describes each figure, then the description is embedded as text.
cons: One LLM call per image at index time
A caption can miss or invent detail
options.bestWhen: Charts and diagrams need explanations and text citations.
options.avoidWhen: Index-time LLM cost is prohibitive or users search by image.

options.name: Single-vector multimodal embedding
options.summary: One vector per image or text, in one space (Azure Vision, Cohere embed, jina-embeddings-v4).
pros: Look-alike search with no LLM at index time
cons: Vectors from different models are not comparable
options.bestWhen: Users search by example image or need look-alikes.
options.avoidWhen: You must justify results with citable text.

options.name: Page-image multi-vector (ColPali family)
options.summary: A VLM embeds each page image into many vectors, and late interaction (MaxSim) scores queries against them.
pros: Strong results on the ViDoRe benchmark
cons: About 30 times the storage of a text vector per page
Evidence is a page image, not text
options.bestWhen: Figure-heavy pages where parsing fails and storage is available.
options.avoidWhen: Tight index budget or text citations are mandatory.

blocks.title: Pick a retrieval approach
blocks.prompt: Change where meaning lives, how users query, the storage budget and the evidence form.

prose.why: Extra LLM cost for little gain.

visual.why: Reads the page as an image.

blocks.takeaway: Text pipelines lead until meaning moves into visuals. Then evidence form and storage budget decide between captions, single vectors and page images.

blocks.title: Two index paths for one page
blocks.alt: A page or image is either verbalized by an LLM into a text index with citations, or embedded directly into a vector index for look-alike search. Both feed a hybrid query.
blocks.src:
flowchart LR
  P[Page or image] --> V[Verbalize with an LLM]
  P --> E[Embed directly]
  V --> T[Text index with citations]
  E --> I[Vector index for look-alike]
  T --> H[Hybrid query]
  I --> H
blocks.caption: Mixed corpora often run both paths side by side.

items.symptom: The right page is retrieved but the answer misquotes a chart
items.cause: Generation misread the figure, and retrieval quality was never measured apart from answer quality
items.fix: Evaluate retrieval and answer separately. Raise image detail or crop the figure for the generator.

items.symptom: Image search finds look-alikes but cannot say why or cite
items.cause: The embedding-only path gives no reasons or citation text
items.fix: Add a verbalization path for the same corpus.

items.symptom: Similarity scores look arbitrary across queries
items.cause: Azure Vision relevance scores do not compare across queries, and vectors from different model versions are not comparable
items.fix: Use per-query ranks, and re-embed the whole corpus when you change the model version.

items.symptom: Index storage balloons after adopting page-image retrieval
items.cause: Multi-vector pages cost about 30 times a text vector
items.fix: Apply compression or token pooling, or restrict it to figure-heavy pages.

items.symptom: Evaluation passes but users keep asking chart questions
items.cause: The golden set is text only
items.fix: Stratify the golden set by modality and report each stratum.

items.title: Go deeper: Azure AI Search multimodal skills

blocks.md: The Content Understanding skill gives cross-page tables, bounding polygons and semantic chunking [[r12]]. Image descriptions in that skill need REST `2026-05-01-preview`. The Document Layout skill stays supported, but new skillsets should use the Content Understanding skill.

Azure Vision multimodal embeddings have 1,024 dimensions, take images under 20 MB between 10 x 10 and 16,000 x 16,000 px and text of 1 to 70 words. Model `2023-04-15` is multilingual and `2022-04-11` is English only [[r13]]. Cohere `embed-v4.0` handles text, images and mixed PDFs with 128k context and dimensions 256, 512, 1024 or 1536 (default) [[r22]]. The newer `embed-v5.0-pro` and `embed-v5.0-fast` offer up to 2048 (default). `jina-embeddings-v4` has 3.8 billion parameters, supports single-vector and multi-vector output with LoRA adapters, and introduced the Jina-VDR benchmark [[r23]].

ColPali uses PaliGemma-3B with 1,024 patches per page projected to 128 dimensions and scores with MaxSim as ColBERT does [[r14]]. ColQwen2 caps patches at 768 and adds 5.3 nDCG@5 over ColPali. The benchmark is ViDoRe. Compression and token pooling cut storage.

Score three layers apart: parse fidelity (was the figure captured), retrieval (page recall at k and element recall) and answer faithfulness to the visual. Build a golden set stratified by modality, compare with a text-only baseline, and use a public benchmark such as ViDoRe only as a sanity check [[r20]]. World w14 covers the metrics.

quiz.q: A page-image index stores about 257.5 KB per page. How many GB does it need for 2 million pages (1 GB = 1,000,000 KB)?
quiz.hint: pages x KB per page, then divide by 1,000,000.
quiz.explain: 2,000,000 x 257.5 KB = 515,000,000 KB, which is 515 GB. The same corpus at 8.6 KB per page of BGE-M3 vectors would need about 17.2 GB, which is the roughly 30 times gap that drives the storage dial.

quiz.q: Users upload a photo of a part and want look-alike parts. Text citations are not required and the index budget is tight. Which approach fits?
options: Single-vector multimodal embeddings, which support image-to-vector queries with one vector per item
Parse then text-embed, because text pipelines are the cheapest way to index and search any collection of pages
Caption then embed, since captions give citable text for every part
Page-image multi-vector retrieval, because it leads on the ViDoRe benchmark
quiz.explain: Image-to-vector queries and look-alike search are the strength of single-vector embeddings, and the cost is one vector per item. A text pipeline cannot take an image query, captions add an LLM call per image for a citation need that does not exist here, and page-image multi-vector costs about 30 times the storage.

quiz.q: Retrieval finds the right page every time, yet answers misquote a chart's axis labels. What is the best next step?
options: Swap in an embedding model with more dimensions so the chart page ranks even higher in the results
Measure retrieval and answer quality apart, then raise image detail or crop the figure
Move to a multi-vector index to improve recall
Lower top k so fewer pages distract the model
quiz.explain: Recall is already fine, so the fault sits in reading the figure. Separate measurement confirms it, and higher detail or a cropped figure helps the generator. Larger embeddings, multi-vector storage and a lower top k all target retrieval, not reading.

takeaways: Text pipelines win until meaning lives in visuals
Verbalizing gives citable text, single vectors give image queries, page images give layout fidelity at about 30 times the storage
Mixed corpora often run two paths side by side
Measure parse, retrieval and answer layers separately, with a golden set stratified by modality
